about: The 2014 Week 8 league roundup's stored text, rendered by runtime/week_pages.py into career/2014/Regular_Season/League_Results/week_08.md under its game headings: each game's highlights and standouts, keyed by the game's event id and written only from that game's compact closed-game receipt (scoring events, drives, team and player statistics, injuries), and the week's reactive events. Jacksonville's game has its own Game Report and no entry here.

games.2014-week08-baltimore-ravens-at-cincinna: Jeremy Hill scored three touchdowns, running for two and catching one of Andy Dalton's two touchdown passes, Cedric Peerman catching the other, and Reggie Nelson intercepted Joe Flacco twice in the second half, the first setting up Mike Nugent's 33-yard field goal for a 17-14 lead early in the fourth quarter and the second giving Cincinnati the ball at the Baltimore 11 for a one-play touchdown drive that made it 31-21 with 2:00 left. Baltimore led 14-7 at the half after touchdown drives of 73 and 67 yards, the second only three plays, and went back ahead 21-17 on a seven-play, 79-yard drive with 4:39 left, but Dalton, who completed 26 of 34 for 281 yards without an interception, answered with an eight-play, 80-yard touchdown drive. Bernard Pierce ran seven times for 93 yards and a touchdown, with a 55-yarder, Flacco ran for another and threw one to Owen Daniels, Torrey Smith caught eight passes for 86 and Terrell Suggs made fifteen tackles with a sack, while Justin Tucker missed from 51 and Nugent from 34 in the second quarter. Standouts: Hill, Nelson, Dalton. Baltimore's Chykie Brown left on a head hold projected at seventeen days, and Cincinnati's Peerman with an injury projected at eight.
games.2014-week08-buffalo-bills-at-new-york-je: Geno Smith threw touchdown passes to Jeremy Kerley, who caught eight of 13 targets for 99 yards, and Chris Ivory, and the Jets scored on three straight possessions, a 10-play, 66-yard drive that tied it at 7, Nick Folk's 35-yard field goal with 58 seconds left in the half and an 11-play, 64-yard drive to open the second half for a 17-7 lead. Kyle Orton's touchdown pass to Robert Woods, who caught eight of 14 targets for 92, had finished an 84-yard drive early in the second quarter, and Duke Williams's interception of Smith gave Buffalo the ball at the New York 36 for the first of Dan Carpenter's field goals, from 20 and 22 yards, the second making it 17-13 with 10:11 left. The Bills' last possession began at their own 45 with 1:26 left and ended on a failed fourth-and-10 at the New York 26; C.J. Spiller ran 21 times for 106 yards, Jordan Gay put five of his seven punts inside the 20 and Buffalo sacked Smith four times without allowing a sack. Standouts: Kerley, Spiller, Woods. Buffalo's Scott Chandler left with an injury projected at thirty-two days, and the Jets' Demario Davis with one projected at four.
games.2014-week08-chicago-bears-at-new-england: Chicago's 12-play, 77-yard touchdown drive with 1:44 left decided it, after Stephen Gostkowski's 32-yard field goal had brought New England within 14-13, and the Patriots' last possession reached the Chicago 19 as time ran out. Jay Cutler threw touchdown passes to Alshon Jeffery and Josh Morgan and Ka'Deem Carey ran for the other, the Bears' 12-play, 95-yard drive from their own 5, after Senorise Perry muffed and recovered a kickoff, putting them ahead 14-10 with 42 seconds left in the half; Alfonzo Dennard's interception of Cutler had set up Stevan Ridley's touchdown run on a four-play, 67-yard drive that tied it at 7. Jerod Mayo made fifteen tackles with a sack and forced both of Chicago's lost fumbles in the third quarter, Chandler Jones and Dont'a Hightower recovering them, but Gostkowski missed from 45 after the first and the Patriots punted after the second, and Tom Brady completed 28 of 41 for 338 yards without a touchdown or an interception, Julian Edelman catching eight of 10 targets for 103. Standouts: Cutler, Mayo, Edelman. Chicago's Tony Fiammetta left on a head hold projected at seventeen days.
games.2014-week08-detroit-lions-at-atlanta-fal: Matt Ryan threw three touchdown passes to Julio Jones, who caught seven of eight targets for 103 yards, and Atlanta scored touchdowns on its first three possessions, drives of 80, 48 and 58 yards, to lead 21-0 after the first quarter; Ryan completed 14 of 19 for 189 without an interception and Steven Jackson ran for the Falcons' other offensive touchdown. Detroit opened the second half with a six-play, 89-yard touchdown drive and, after a punt, went 83 yards in 13 plays, scoring on fourth-and-1 from the 1, to get within 21-14 late in the third quarter, Matthew Stafford throwing touchdown passes to Calvin Johnson, who caught six for 129 with a 71-yarder, and Corey Fuller. Atlanta answered with an 86-yard touchdown drive in five plays, and Paul Worrilow's strip sack, which he recovered and returned 19 yards for a touchdown with 3:23 left, made it 35-14; the Falcons sacked Stafford five times, Joplo Bartu twice, and Kemal Ishmael intercepted him on Detroit's next possession. Standouts: Jones, Ryan, Worrilow.
games.2014-week08-green-bay-packers-at-new-orl: Shayne Graham's 20-yard field goal finished New Orleans's nine-play, 65-yard drive on the first possession of overtime, and Green Bay's answer reached the New Orleans 24 before Mason Crosby missed from 42; Crosby had forced overtime with a 48-yard field goal as time expired, after Graham's 38-yarder with 33 seconds left had finished a nine-play, 79-yard drive that began at the New Orleans 1. Drew Brees completed 29 of 38 for 334 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, two to Jimmy Graham and one each to Brandin Cooks, who caught 10 of 12 targets for 169, and Austin Johnson, Khiry Robinson ran 13 times for 107 and the Saints held the ball more than 40 minutes, a 14-play, 80-yard drive tying it at 28 with 5:25 left. Aaron Rodgers threw for 366 yards and three touchdowns, a 60-yarder to Brandon Bostick that tied it at 7 on the first snap after a kickoff, a second to Bostick and one to Jordy Nelson, Eddie Lacy ran for another and DuJuan Harris's 77-yard kickoff return set up the touchdown that put Green Bay ahead 28-21 early in the fourth quarter, but the Packers lost three fumbles, Randall Cobb's on a punt return, Harris's at the New Orleans 8 and Jarrett Boykin's at the New Orleans 30. Standouts: Brees, Cooks, Bostick. New Orleans's Cameron Jordan left with an injury projected at thirteen days.
games.2014-week08-houston-texans-at-tennessee-: Tennessee led 27-3 with 1:13 left in the half after Ryan Succop's field goals from 29 and 49 yards and three touchdown drives, the second a three-play drive after Jason McCourty intercepted Ryan Fitzpatrick to give the Titans the ball at the Houston 21 and the third a five-play, 74-yard drive in 54 seconds; Jake Locker threw touchdown passes to Kendall Wright, who caught 13 of 17 targets for 175 yards, Justin Hunter and Craig Stevens, and Shonn Greene ran 14 times for 91 yards and a touchdown. Houston scored with one second left in the half on a four-play, 86-yard drive and, after Kendrick Lewis intercepted Locker on the first snap of a Tennessee possession to give the Texans the ball at the Tennessee 42, got within 34-27 with 1:10 left in the third quarter; Fitzpatrick completed 33 of 46 for 422 yards with touchdown passes to DeAndre Hopkins and Garrett Graham, who caught seven for 107, and Damaris Johnson ran for the third touchdown. The Texans' 14-play drive in the fourth quarter converted a fourth-and-4 at the Tennessee 10 but ended on a failed fourth-and-12 at the 12 with 1:19 left, and their last possession reached the Tennessee 40 as time ran out; Houston converted two of 12 third downs, and Zach Brown made thirteen tackles with a sack. Standouts: Wright, Fitzpatrick, Locker. Tennessee's Bernard Pollard left on a head hold projected at eleven days.
games.2014-week08-indianapolis-colts-at-pittsb: Shaun Suisham's 35-yard field goal with 34 seconds left, his third, decided it, after Adam Vinatieri's 42-yarder had brought Indianapolis within 13-10 with 3:28 left, in a game of six turnovers, three by each club. Vontae Davis intercepted Ben Roethlisberger twice, returning one 15 yards for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, and Bjoern Werner once, while Jason Worilds and Ryan Shazier intercepted Andrew Luck and Shazier forced a fumble on a sack that Stephon Tuitt recovered, giving Pittsburgh the ball at the Indianapolis 42 for the first of Suisham's field goals. Roethlisberger's touchdown pass to Lance Moore finished an eight-play, 55-yard drive after Luck's second interception and made it 13-0 late in the third quarter; Luck completed 28 of 46 for 244 yards, T.Y. Hilton catching 11 of 13 targets for 101 and Reggie Wayne eight for 70, and the Colts converted eight of 16 third downs but drew twelve penalties for 108 yards. Standouts: Shazier, Davis, Suisham. Pittsburgh's Ramon Foster left on a head hold projected at seventeen days and Cam Thomas on one projected at three.
games.2014-week08-minnesota-vikings-at-tampa-b: Matt Cassel completed 19 of 24 for 247 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, to Adrian Peterson, Charles Johnson and Greg Jennings, and Matt Asiata ran for another as Minnesota scored touchdowns on four of its 10 possessions, the third, after a punt from the Buccaneers' 5, a three-play drive from the Tampa Bay 36 that made it 21-13 in the third quarter and the fourth an 83-yard drive in five plays for a 28-16 lead with 9:10 left. Tampa Bay held the ball more than 36 minutes, had 28 first downs and converted nine of 16 third downs, Patrick Murray kicking field goals from 56, 55 and 27 yards, the 55-yarder as the first half ended, and Doug Martin ran for one touchdown and Russell Shepard caught the other from Josh McCown, Tampa Bay answering Minnesota's last touchdown with a seven-play, 84-yard drive that made it 28-23 with 6:31 left. The Buccaneers' last possession, 12 plays from their own 10 with 3:18 left, ended on a failed fourth-and-10 at the Minnesota 14 with 18 seconds left; Peterson ran 18 times for 80 yards, with a 48-yarder, and caught four passes for 56, Tampa Bay drew ten penalties for 94 yards and Minnesota sacked McCown four times. Standouts: Cassel, Peterson, Murray. Minnesota's John Sullivan left with an injury projected at thirty-eight days, Jasper Brinkley with one projected at eighteen and Kyle Rudolph on a head hold projected at three.
games.2014-week08-oakland-raiders-at-cleveland: Oakland took the ball away nine times, intercepting Brian Hoyer five times and recovering four fumbles, one of them on a muffed punt, and every one of its 51 points came on or after a takeaway, from Tarell Brown's 15-yard interception return for a touchdown with 9:45 left to touchdown drives that began at the Cleveland 43, 15 and 7. Khalil Mack sacked Hoyer four times and intercepted him once, Brown intercepted him twice and Charles Woodson and Miles Burris once each, and Derek Carr completed 23 of 29 for 225 yards and four touchdowns, to Rod Streater, who caught eight for 71, Andre Holmes, Denarius Moore and Darren McFadden, who also ran 23 times for 123 yards and a touchdown. Cleveland's touchdowns came on Hoyer's pass to Marqise Lee at the end of a 12-play, 76-yard drive that made it 10-7 in the second quarter and on Barkevious Mingo's 75-yard return of Streater's fumble, which Mingo forced, with 33 seconds left; Mingo also had two sacks among his twelve tackles, and Phillip Taylor forced and recovered Carr's fumble on a sack at the Cleveland 19. Standouts: Mack, Carr, Brown. Cleveland's Taylor left on a head hold projected at twenty-seven days.
games.2014-week08-philadelphia-eagles-at-arizo: Carson Palmer completed 22 of 31 for 403 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, Larry Fitzgerald catching nine of 10 targets for 133 and John Carlson two passes for 115, one a 72-yarder, and Arizona scored touchdowns on its first two possessions, drives of 86 and 89 yards, and on three of its five possessions in the second half, the last ending with two seconds left. Jonathan Dwyer ran for two touchdowns and caught one, finishing with 64 rushing yards and five catches for 101, Fitzgerald and Michael Floyd caught the other two touchdown passes and Antonio Cromartie returned an interception of Nick Foles 44 yards for a touchdown that made it 35-3 with 6:05 left. Philadelphia's only points came on Cody Parkey's field goal with 24 seconds left in the half; the Eagles converted one of 11 third downs, Foles completed 15 of 29 for 117 yards and was sacked three times, twice by Matt Shaughnessy, Donnie Jones punted nine times, six inside the 20, and DeMeco Ryans recovered Palmer's fumble at the Philadelphia 4 in the third quarter. Standouts: Palmer, Dwyer, Fitzgerald. Arizona's Palmer left with an injury projected at twenty days, Tony Jefferson on a head hold projected at six and Dwyer on one with no time projected lost, and Philadelphia's Brandon Graham on one with no time projected lost.
games.2014-week08-san-diego-chargers-at-denver: Brandon McManus's 55-yard field goal with 1:31 left made it 35-29, after Chris Harris forced Ryan Mathews's fumble on the Chargers' first snap following a kickoff and Derek Wolfe recovered at the San Diego 35, and San Diego's last possession went 79 yards in seven plays to the Denver 1 before time ran out. Montee Ball ran 22 times for 182 yards, with a 55-yarder, and ran in the two-point conversion after the four-play, 50-yard touchdown drive that put the Broncos ahead 32-29 with 3:33 left, on the possession after they failed on fourth-and-6 at the San Diego 6, and Brock Osweiler threw two touchdown passes to Julius Thomas and one to Demaryius Thomas, Ronnie Hillman running for the other touchdown. Denver led 14-0 in the first quarter, the second touchdown three plays after Kayvon Webster's interception gave it the ball at the San Diego 13, but Philip Rivers, who threw for 316 yards, answered on the Chargers' next snap with an 80-yard touchdown pass to Keenan Allen, who caught six for 141, and threw another to Mathews to finish a 12-play, 80-yard drive for a 26-24 lead early in the fourth quarter; Osweiler was intercepted twice and lost a fumble on a sack that Kavell Conner forced and recovered, setting up the third of Nick Novak's five field goals as the half ended. Standouts: Ball, Allen, Novak.
games.2014-week08-seattle-seahawks-at-carolina: Carolina sacked Tarvaris Jackson nine times, Luke Kuechly and Thomas Davis three times each, and took the ball away on Seattle's first snap, when Greg Hardy's strip sack was recovered by Charles Johnson to give the Panthers the ball at the Seattle 42 for the first of Graham Gano's four field goals, from 44, 50, 51 and 21 yards. Cam Newton completed 24 of 36 for 321 yards without an interception, Kelvin Benjamin catching nine of 13 targets for 133 and his touchdown pass, and DeAngelo Williams ran 21 times for 130 yards and a touchdown; Carolina's 10-play, 91-yard drive made it 13-3 in the second quarter, and Roman Harper's interception on the first snap of Seattle's next-to-last possession set up a three-play touchdown drive from the Seattle 43 for a 26-6 lead with 1:53 left. Stephen Hauschka's field goals from 24 and 40 yards were Seattle's only points, the Seahawks failed on fourth-and-10 at their own 47 with 6:21 left, and Malcolm Smith forced Williams's fumble at the Seattle 4 in the third quarter, Jeremy Lane recovering. Standouts: Davis, Kuechly, Benjamin. Carolina's Benjamin left with an injury projected at 120 days and Harper with one projected at nine, and Seattle's Smith on a head hold projected at three.
games.2014-week08-st-louis-rams-at-kansas-city: Shaun Hill threw touchdown passes to Lance Kendricks, who caught all six of his targets for 144 yards with a 77-yarder, Jared Cook and Kenny Britt, and Greg Zuerlein made all four of his field goals, from 35, 23, 38 and 36 yards, as St. Louis did not turn the ball over and Kansas City lost four; the Rams' three-play, 80-yard drive answered the Chiefs' own three-play, 80-yard drive, which had pulled Kansas City within 26-24, to make it 33-24 with 11:55 left. Janoris Jenkins intercepted Alex Smith twice and Trumaine Johnson once; the interception on the game's first possession gave the Rams the ball at the Kansas City 2, though they lost 14 yards and settled for Zuerlein's first field goal, and another, after the Chiefs had reached the St. Louis 11, set up a five-play touchdown drive from the Kansas City 35 for a 17-7 lead. Donnie Avery caught nine of 12 targets for 209 yards and two touchdowns, with a 73-yarder, and Jamaal Charles ran for Kansas City's other touchdown, but after the Rams failed on fourth-and-10 at the Kansas City 21 with 6:08 left, Brandon McGee forced Avery's fumble and James Laurinaitis recovered, and the Chiefs' last possession ended in Smith's third interception with 1:56 left. Standouts: Kendricks, Avery, Jenkins.
games.2014-week08-washington-redskins-at-dalla: Washington took the overtime kickoff and drove 77 yards in 11 plays for the winning touchdown, after Dan Bailey's 32-yard field goal as time expired had tied it at 19 to finish a seven-play, 67-yard drive on which Washington was penalized twice for 50 yards. Kai Forbath made all four of his field goals, from 27, from 59 on the last play of the first half, from 34 and from 33, the last for a 19-16 lead with 1:40 left, and Bailey made all four of his, from 33, 21, 41 and 32 yards. Robert Griffin completed 23 of 36 for 277 yards without an interception and threw touchdown passes to DeSean Jackson and Santana Moss, Washington's first score finishing a 12-play, 76-yard drive that took 8:32 after Dallas failed on fourth-and-1 at the Washington 24, while Tony Romo's only touchdown pass, to Terrance Williams, finished a four-play, 80-yard drive in 48 seconds that tied it at 10 before the half and E.J. Biggers intercepted Romo after the Cowboys reached the Washington 7 in the third quarter; DeMarco Murray ran 19 times for 69 yards and caught four passes for 94. Standouts: Griffin, Forbath, Murray. Washington's Shawn Lauvao left on a head hold projected at three days.

reactive_events: None recorded. No trade demand, coaching story or locker-room event follows from a logged Week 8 game event or a recorded transaction, and the Week 8 head-coach check made no change.
